Rashi on Eruvin 68b:10:1.hebrew: מי שנתן רשותו - לבני חצר, מפני ששכח ולא עירב; ולאחר שביטל הוציא מביתו לחצר — אוסר על בני חצר, דהדר שקליה לרשותיה:
Rashi on Eruvin 68b:10:1.english: One who gave his rights - To the residents of the courtyard, because he forgot and did not join in the eiruv; and after he renounced [them], he carried [an item] out from his house into the courtyard — he renders [carrying] prohibited for the residents of the courtyard, for he has taken back his rights.

Rashi on Eruvin 68b:10:2.hebrew: ר"מ - דאמר: אפילו בשוגג הדרא ליה רשותיה — סבר: לא מסולק הוא, וגבי ביטול נמי חוזרין ומבטלין, והדרא ליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 68b:10:2.english: Rabbi Meir - Who said that even [if he carried out] unwittingly, his rights return to him, holds that he is not [completely] removed; and with regard to renunciation as well, [residents] may go back and renounce [their rights in his favor], and it returns to him.

Rashi on Eruvin 68b:12:1.hebrew: לא דכ"ע אין חוזרין ומבטלין - דאיסתלק ליה, ובדין הוא דבשוגג לא הדרא ליה, אלא ר"מ קניס שוגג אטו מזיד. ובמזיד כולהו מודו דאף על גב דאיסתלק ליה — כיון דהדר, הדר, דהא לא זבניה; וכגון שלא החזיקו בני מבוי במבוי לאחר ביטול קודם חזרה:
Rashi on Eruvin 68b:12:1.english: No, everyone agrees that one may not renounce and then renounce again - For he has removed himself [from his domain], and strictly speaking, in [the case of an] unwitting [act, his rights] should not return to him; rather, Rabbi Meir penalizes an unwitting [act] on account of an intentional [act]. And in [the case of an] intentional [act], all agree that even though he removed himself, once he retracts, he has retracted, for he did not sell it [to them]; and [this is] in a case where the residents of the alleyway did not take possession of the alleyway after the renunciation [and] before the retraction.

Rashi on Eruvin 68b:14:1.hebrew: צדוקי מאן דכר שמיה - מי קאמר ת"ק דבעי למיגר, דפליג רבן גמליאל ואמר דיכול לבטל:
Rashi on Eruvin 68b:14:1.english: A Sadducee; who mentioned his name? - Did the First Tanna say that one needs to rent [from a Sadducee], such that Rabban Gamliel disagrees and says that he can renounce [his rights]?

Rashi on Eruvin 68b:15:1.english: He is like a gentile - For he cannot renounce [his rights] without leasing [them].

Rashi on Eruvin 68b:15:2.hebrew: והוציאו את הכלים - והחזיקו במבוי, ושוב לא יוכל לחזור מביטולו. וכשקדש היום עסקינן, דחזקה דמבעוד יום לא מוכחא:
Rashi on Eruvin 68b:15:2.english: And take out the utensils - And take possession of the alleyway, and then he will no longer be able to retract his renunciation. And we are dealing with [a case where] the day had [already] become sanctified, for an act of possession [performed] while it is still day is not evident.

Rashi on Eruvin 68b:16:1.english: And it is taught [in a baraita] - [This is stated] in an affirmative tone: that the Rabbis disagree regarding a Sadducee.

Rashi on Eruvin 68b:16:2.hebrew: עד שלא יוציא - כליו במבוי, ויחזור ויטול את רשותו:
Rashi on Eruvin 68b:16:2.english: Before he takes out - his utensils into the alleyway, and retracts and reclaims his domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 68b:17:1.hebrew: ועשו צורכיכם - מבעוד יום, עד שלא תחשך. קסבר ר' יהודה: דלא פליג רבן גמליאל, אלא צדוקי כנכרי ס"ל, ואין יכול לבטל. ולקמן פריך: והתנן לרבי יהודה ״עד שלא יוציא״, אלמא לר' יהודה אליבא דרבן גמליאל יכול הוא לבטל, ובהא הוא דפליג רבי יהודה — דקסבר לאחר חזקה נמי יכול לחזור בו:
Rashi on Eruvin 68b:17:1.english: And do whatever you must do - [Meaning,] while it is still day, before night falls. Rabbi Yehuda maintains that Rabban Gamliel does not disagree [with the first Tanna], but rather holds that a Sadducee is like a gentile, and [therefore] cannot renounce [his rights]. And later, [the Gemara] challenges: But didn't we learn [in the Mishnah], according to Rabbi Yehuda, "before he takes out"? Evidently, according to Rabbi Yehuda in the view of Rabban Gamliel, he can renounce [his rights], and it is in this that Rabbi Yehuda disagrees [with Rabbi Meir] — for he maintains that even after possession [has been established], he can still retract.

Rashi on Eruvin 68b:1:1.hebrew: ניתיב מר אדוכתיה - דמדקאמרת: "פנו לי מאני", גלית אדעתך דמאחר שתבטל רשותך אין לך היום היתר בחצר. והיינו כשמואל, דאמר לקמן: "אין מבטלין וחוזרין ומבטלין". דאי לאו כשמואל סבירא לך, ליתיב מר אדוכתיה, ובטל להם רשות חצרך שעה אחת עד שיקחו החמין, ויחזרו הם ויבטלו לך אותו הרשות, ויחזירו לך חצרך:
Rashi on Eruvin 68b:1:1.english: Let the Master remain in his place - For since you said, “Clear my items for me,” you revealed your thinking that once you renounce your domain, you have no permission [to carry] in the courtyard today, and this is in accordance with [the view of] Shmuel, who said below: “One may not renounce and then renounce [again].” For if you did not hold in accordance with Shmuel, let the Master remain in his place and renounce the domain of your courtyard to them for one hour until they take the hot water, and then let them renounce that domain back to you and return your courtyard to you.

Rashi on Eruvin 68b:1:2.hebrew: דהא אמר רב מבטלין וחוזרין ומבטלין - שנים הדרין בחצר אחת ולא עירבו, מבטל זה רשותו לזה עד שיעשה צרכיו, ויחזור זה ויבטל לזה:
Rashi on Eruvin 68b:1:2.english: For Rav said: One may renounce and then renounce again - [If] two [people] dwell in one courtyard and did not make an eiruv, this one renounces his domain to that one until he attends to his needs, and that one may then renounce [it back] to this one.

Rashi on Eruvin 68b:3:1.english: The Master, too, should not renounce [his rights] - For this is [a renunciation] from one courtyard to another.

Rashi on Eruvin 68b:4:1.hebrew: התם - דאין חוזרין ומבטלין, טעמא לאו משום דה"ל כבן חצר אחרת, אלא משום דלא ליהוי מילי דרבנן:
Rashi on Eruvin 68b:4:1.english: There - [Regarding the rule] that they do not renounce and renounce again, the reason is not because he has become like a resident of another courtyard, but rather so that the words of the Sages should not be [a laughingstock].

Rashi on Eruvin 68b:7:1.hebrew: רב דאמר כרבנן - דאמרי במתני': ביתו אסור להכניס ולהוציא לו ולהם, דאמרי: המבטל רשות חצירו לא ביטל רשות ביתו. אלמא לא מסתלק ליה לגמרי, ולא הוה ליה כבן חצר אחרת:
Rashi on Eruvin 68b:7:1.english: Rav stated [his ruling] in accordance with the Rabbis - Who say in the Mishnah [that with regard to] his house, it is forbidden to bring in and take out [objects], for him and for them, as they say: One who renounces the rights to his courtyard has not renounced the rights to his house. Evidently, he has not completely removed himself, and he is not [considered] like a resident of another courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 68b:7:2.hebrew: ושמואל כרבי אליעזר - דאמר בפרק עושין פסין (לעיל עירובין דף כו:): ביתו מותר להכניס ולהוציא להם, מאחר שביטל רשותו — דרשות ביתו נמי ביטל:
Rashi on Eruvin 68b:7:2.english: And Shmuel [holds] in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer - who said in the chapter [entitled] Osin Passin (above, Eruvin 26b): [With regard to] his house, it is permitted to bring in and take out [objects] for them, since he renounced his rights — for the rights to his house he also renounced.

Rashi on Eruvin 68b:8:1.hebrew: אבל לענין איסתלוקי - לשוויה נפשיה כבן חצר אחרת, דלא לימצי למהדר וקבולי רשותיה — מי אמר:
Rashi on Eruvin 68b:8:1.english: However, with regard to removal - To make himself like a resident of another courtyard, so that he cannot return and receive rights — did he say [this]?

Rashi on Eruvin 68b:9:1.hebrew: אבל מאי דבטיל מיהא איסתלק לגמרי - מן החצר שביטל בפירוש — ודאי איסתלק, וה"ל כבן חצר אחרת:
Rashi on Eruvin 68b:9:1.english: However, from that which he renounced, at least he has removed himself completely - From the courtyard that he explicitly renounced, he has certainly removed himself, and he is like a resident of another courtyard.

Tosafot on Eruvin 68b:12:1.hebrew: קנסו שוגג אטו מזיד - לא שייך לקנסו שוגג אטו מזיד דעלמא, דהכא לא קנסי' לדידיה מידי, דבלאו הכי הוה אסיר; אלא כלומר: גזרו שוגג אטו מזיד:
Tosafot on Eruvin 68b:12:1.english: They penalized an unwitting [offender] due to an intentional [offender] - [This] does not pertain to the general [principle of] "they penalized an unwitting [offender] due to an intentional [offender]," for here we do not penalize him in any way, since even without this he was [already] forbidden [to carry]; rather, it means to say: They decreed [an] unwitting [act] due to [an] intentional [act].

Tosafot on Eruvin 68b:13:1.hebrew: רב אשי אמר רב ושמואל בפלוגתא דרבי אליעזר כו' - לית ליה לרב אשי הא דאמר רבא לעיל אליבא דשמואל: "פעמים מבטלין ופעמים אין מבטלין"; דהא מסיק לעיל כי קאמר — לרבנן, והכא לרב אשי, הוה שמואל כרבי אליעזר:
Tosafot on Eruvin 68b:13:1.english: "Rav Ashi said: Rav and Shmuel disagree in the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer, etc." - Rav Ashi does not accept that which Rava said above according to Shmuel: "Sometimes one may renounce, and sometimes one may not renounce"; for [the Gemara] concluded above that when [Shmuel] stated [his opinion, it was] according to the Rabbis, whereas here, according to Rav Ashi, Shmuel was [holding] in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer.

Tosafot on Eruvin 68b:14:1.english: "Rabban Gamliel said: There was an incident involving a Sadducee, etc." - I explained [this] in [the commentary on] our Mishnah.

Tosafot on Eruvin 68b:16:1.hebrew: והתניא - בניחותא, ומייתי סיועא דפליגי רבנן בצדוקי. אבל מכל מקום, בברייתא זו צ"ל חסורי מיחסרא, שלא יהא מעשה לסתור. ואינו נראה כלל לחלק משום דמתני' סתמא קתני, אבל בברייתא מסיים בה: "דברי ר"מ", שהיה שונה דברי רבותיו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 68b:16:1.english: "And wasn’t it taught" - [This is stated] affirmatively, and it brings support [to the statement] that the Rabbis disagree concerning a Sadducee. However, in any case, in this baraita one must say that it is incomplete [ḥasorei meḥasra], so that it will not be an incident that contradicts [the rule that precedes it]. And it does not appear at all [plausible] to differentiate [between the Mishnah and the baraita] on the grounds that the Mishnah taught anonymously, whereas the baraita concludes with "the statement of Rabbi Meir," who was reciting the words of his teachers.

Tosafot on Eruvin 68b:16:2.hebrew: והוציאו מה שאתם מוציאין והכניסו מה כו' - פירוש: או הכניסו, דבחד מינייהו הוי חזקה, כשעושה דבר שהיה נאסר בלא ביטול. והא דקתני בסמוך: "מי שנתן רשותו והוציא, בין בשוגג בין במזיד — אוסר", לאו דוקא הוציא, אלא אפילו הכניס:
Tosafot on Eruvin 68b:16:2.english: "And take out what you take out, and bring in what..." - Explanation: [It means] or "bring in," for with [either] one of them an act of acquisition [chazakah] is established, when one performs an action that would have been prohibited without renunciation [of rights]. And that which is taught nearby: "One who relinquished his domain and took out [an item], whether unwittingly or intentionally, prohibits [the others]" — [it is] not specifically [if he] took out [an item], but rather even [if he] brought [one] in.

Tosafot on Eruvin 68b:18:1.hebrew: למימרא דכי מפקי אינהו כו' - מתוך הלשון משמע דמסיק אדעתיה שפיר לחלק בין מפיק אינהו והדר מפיק איהו, למפיק איהו ברישא. ותימה: דאם כן, מאי קא קשיא ליה? הא איכא לאוקומי מתני' ד"מי שנתן רשותו כו'" כגון דמפיק איהו ברישא, כדמשני אביי "כאן שהחזיקו"! ואין לומר ד"מי שנתן רשותו והוציא" משמע ליה בכל ענין שהוציא, אפילו דמפקי ליה אינהו ברישא — דהא כי משני רב יוסף "אימא אינו אוסר", ע"כ לאו בכל ענין קתני, דהא בעי למימר: כי מפיק איהו ברישא — אוסר. ומפרש ר"י: ד"מי שנתן רשותו" משמע ליה שנגמרה לגמרי מתנתו, דהיינו כי החזיקו, דאפקי אינהו ברישא, מדלא קתני "מי שביטל", דמשמע אמירה בעלמא, כדקתני לעיל: "שהרי ביטל לכם רשותו". ואביי, דמוקי לה בשלא החזיקו, קא סבר דשייך למיתני "מי שנתן" אף על גב דאיירי בלא החזיקו, ומייתי סייעתא מברייתא דקתני "מי שנתן" וקתני סיפא: "בד"א — בשלא החזיקו". אבל להא לא אצטריכא ליה לאביי לאתויי ראיה, לחלק בין החזיקו ללא החזיקו — דמברייתא דלעיל שמעי' ליה, דקתני: "מהרו והוציאו כו' עד שלא יוציא הוא כו'", ומאי אולמיה דהא מהאי:
Tosafot on Eruvin 68b:18:1.english: Is that to say that when they take out, etc. - From the phrasing [of the Gemara], it implies that [the questioner] well had in mind to distinguish between [a case where] they take out [first] and then he takes out, and [a case where] he takes out first. And [this is] astonishing: for if so, what was difficult to him? Why, it is possible to establish the mishna of "one who gave his rights, etc." as [referring to a case] where he took out first, as Abaye answers: "Here, where they took possession [and there, where they did not take possession]"! And one cannot say that "one who gave his rights and took out" implied to him [that he prohibits] in any circumstance that he took out, even if they had taken out [utensils] first — for behold, when Rav Yosef answers: "Say: 'He does not render it prohibited,'" perforce it is not taught [as applying] in all circumstances, for behold, he wishes to say that when he takes out first, he [does] render it prohibited! And the Ri explains: "One who gave (she-natan) his rights" implied to him that his gift was completely finalized, which is when they took possession — namely, that they took out [utensils] first — since it does not teach "one who renounced" (she-bitel), which would imply a mere statement, as it taught above: "for he renounced his rights in your favor." And Abaye, who establishes it as [referring to a case] where they did not take possession, holds that it is appropriate to teach "one who gave" even though it deals with [a case where] they did not take possession; and he brings support from a baraita that teaches "one who gave" and teaches in the concluding clause: "In what case is this statement said? Where they had not taken possession." However, for this Abaye did not need to bring proof — to distinguish between [where] they took possession and [where] they did not take possession — for from the baraita above we learn it, which teaches: "Hurry and take out, etc., before he takes out, etc."; and what makes this [baraita] stronger than that [one]?

Tosafot on Eruvin 68b:8:1.hebrew: אנא דאמרי אפילו כרבנן - הוה מצי למימר טעמא דלעיל: דלא ליהוו מילי דרבנן כי חוכא ואטלולא:
Tosafot on Eruvin 68b:8:1.english: "What I said is even in accordance with the Rabbis" - [Shmuel] could have stated the reason [given] above: that the words of the Sages should not be like laughter and mockery.
